claims.summary: For d>=4 in characteristic different from two, the exact dimension-six two-pair limit is a codimension-24 subspace Y_d of L((8d-6)H) on the elliptic three-root cover. Its length-(32d-48) Hasse normality is equivalent to invertibility of the 24 branch/top-coefficient conditions on L((8d-6)H-(32d-48)P). If (8d-12)H-(32d-48)P is nonprincipal, four coordinate rows eliminate to a 20-by-20 map. No determinant nonvanishing is asserted.
claims.assessment: Working reduction by exact normalization of both paired blocks, character polynomial bounds, Hasse remainder conditions and genus-one Riemann–Roch. Independent exact degree-four controls compare the direct series, table, 24-row map and 20-row elimination in characteristics 3, 5 and 7.
claims.rationale: Retains the original dimension-six marked source in a bounded determinant independent of degree; it supplies the next normality test without claiming that test passed in every degree.
claims.next_action: Compute and analyze the coupled 20-condition map on the Hasse Tate basis; prove nonvanishing or identify and repair its exact exceptional family.

claims.summary: On the Tate curve over k(u)((rho)), char(k)!=2, with q=rho^2, H=E[2], P=[u], m,r>=1, N=4m and Q=u^N, the 4r functions G(z) times x^j HasseDerivative_j(K_Q)(x) at x=z/h, h in H and 0<=j<r, form a basis of L((m+r)H-NP). Here G=z^(-m)Theta(z/u)^N/Theta(z^2)^m and K_Q=ThetaPrime(1)Theta(Qx)/(Theta(Q)Theta(x)).
claims.assessment: Working proof from automorphy, the unit leading Hasse principal coefficient (-1)^j, degree-zero nonprincipality and a triangular principal-part matrix. Extends the existing three-level Euler basis to arbitrary depth without factorial losses at small primes.
claims.rationale: Provides the characteristic-safe six-level basis required by the dimension-six determinant. It is an explicit extension of the existing theta construction, not a new assertion of determinant nonvanishing.
claims.next_action: Use m=8d-12 and r=6 to construct the full dimension-six marked matrix.

relationships: Uses the exact safe two-pair limiting spaces and sequential transfer to the original series.
Uses the root-cover infinity divisor as the two-torsion coset and marked Tate realization.
Extends the existing automorphy and principal-part construction by replacing Euler powers with Hasse derivatives.
Provides the next dimension-six sufficient determinant test; the general normality claim remains open.
